title: Day 39 · Week 5, Day 4 — Adventure: heat and hydration — the one line that matters, what seventy studies found, and how to run a hot trip with a five-week embryo
summary: The second Adventure episode: the summer trip, the festival, the hot hike. Your baby is 3–5 mm at the turn to Carnegie stage 12, the neural tube sealing at both ends this week and the arm buds appearing; today is also the mean day of onset of pregnancy sickness. Her thermostat: core temperature is highest in the first trimester (37.1 °C at 8 weeks) and falls through pregnancy, with the neutral room temperature dropping 4 °C by 36 weeks (Hartgill 2011); a hot exposure raises maternal core temperature by 0.5 °C, maternal heart rate by 38 bpm and fetal heart rate by 13 bpm on pooled data from 201,906 women (Bonell 2026). The line: 39.0 °C is the teratogenic threshold behind the Day 36 neural-tube evidence, and in 12 studies of 347 pregnant women under exercise and heat no one reached it — land exercise averaged 38.3 °C, max 38.9 (Ravanelli 2019), whose limits (35 min at 80–90% HRmax at 25 °C; water ≤33.4 °C for 45 min; 40 °C bath or 70 °C sauna for 20 min) keep her under it; the CDC's heat-stroke line, 103 °F, is the same temperature from her side. The weather: heatwaves raise preterm birth odds 16% and stillbirth 5% per °C, mostly in late pregnancy, with 'relatively small' summary effects (Chersich 2020, 70 studies); in the first trimester, 10+ days ≥30 °C in weeks 2–8 post-conception add about one heart defect per 1,000 births, concentrated in atrial septal defects (Auger 2017, 704,209 fetuses); miscarriage odds ratios of 1.1–1.2 with intervals touching one (Wesselink 2024; Xu 2025; Das 2023). Water: 2.3 L/day total (EFSA) to 3.0 L (IOM), 70–80% from drinks; the urine colour chart validated in pregnancy — 1–3 fine, ≥4 drink (McKenzie & Armstrong 2017). The field manual: timing, exertion, water, the CDC fan rule (not above 90 °F), cool rooms, the two symptom sets (heat exhaustion vs heat stroke) and the first-trimester trap of mistaking heat illness for pregnancy symptoms.
action: Tonight, ten minutes. Fill a one-litre insulated bottle, put it where her keys live, and agree the rule: it goes everywhere she goes and comes home empty twice a day. Save a picture of the urine colour chart to both phones next to the PUQE score from Day 37 — four means drink. Then open the heat forecast for the next trip or hot weekend: if it is in the top categories, move the hard parts of the day to before ten and after six, keep hard efforts to the cool hours, and find the air conditioning in advance. Hot tubs and saunas stay off the list until Day 42; the pool is the answer.
